newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--With last night's announcement of a new Socialist prime minister for Albania, Albanian President Sali Berisha has attempted to find a compromise with the opposition and break the hold of the rebels on the south of the country. The rebels however appeared unconvinced.

--Despite good relations between Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Italy's Romani Prodi, the Italian government is attempting to keep Greece out of the handling of the Albanian problem, with the Italian press criticising Athens for its support of Berisha.
--The labour and national economy ministries are to cooperate to find a happy half-way point between the government's desire to deregulate the labour market and relations and industrial peace.
--An Athens court today will decide on the legality of the continuing eight-week strike by secondary school teachers: teachers' unions are awaiting the ruling before making any other decisions.
--The south is placing conditions, despite the appointment of Socialist and local boy Bashkim Fino to prime minister: the rebels want participation in talks, and Berisha to resign.
--Athens is sending humanitarian aid to Albania via a battleship: the aid will reach Sarande today or tomorrow.
--The government and social bodies will attempt to find a way to save sinking social security funds in social dialogue scheduled to begin in April.
--The "Apollon Express" braved gale force winds to sail from Santorini to Ios to bring a 24-day-old baby to Athens for treatment for a blood disease.

--Get-rich-quick schemes have raised their ugly heads in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, as three pyramid investment schemes crash and the Albanian chaos threatens to spread. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
